title: Geo-segmented analytics replication policy and tenant-region controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a geo-segmented replication and enforcement policy for Console usage analytics so that tenant events can be scoped, replicated, and retained only within allowed regions. This ticket covers backend routing changes, ingestion pipeline replication controls, tenant configuration surface, and migration tooling for existing tenants that need region isolation.
background: Customers in regulated industries have requested deterministic guarantees that analytics events and derived telemetry remain within approved regions. Current analytics pipelines replicate to multiple regions for availability, but there is no tenant-level opt-out or enforced residency. This causes compliance risk and blocks some customers from using Console analytics features.
proposed_solution: Introduce a tenant attribute 'region_affinity' (regional code(s) or 'global'). Default remains 'global' for existing tenants.
Add routing layer that tags events with region_affinity at the ingestion proxy and rejects cross-region fans when tenant policy forbids it.
Implement per-tenant topic routing: create regional Kafka topics (analytics-<region>-events) and write policies that only allow writes/replication according to tenant affinities.
Extend the streaming replication worker to honor a whitelist/blacklist matrix for inter-region replication; replication runs only for tenants with 'global' or multi-region consent.

Store and audit policy decisions in the Console control plane (encrypted at rest, KMS-backed). Expose a Console setting and API to change region_affinity with approval workflow for high-impact changes.
Provide a migration mode that streams existing historical events into new regional topics for tenants opting into region isolation, with hooks to backfill dashboards and aggregates.
Add enforcement tests and a simulation harness to validate that no sanctioned tenant data appears in disallowed regions under fault scenarios (broker failure, replay, consumer rebalances).
acceptance_criteria: Tenant can set region_affinity via Console UI and admin API.
Ingestion proxies tag events and route to regional topics; no cross-region replication occurs for region-restricted tenants.
Audit trail exists for every cross-region replication decision; records include tenant, event id, source region, destination region, policy version.
Migration tooling can backfill up to 90 days of historical events for a tenant into regional topics with a verified checksum match.
End-to-end performance impact on median ingestion latency < 10% for region-restricted path; 99th percentile SLOs documented.
Security review completed and sign-off from compliance; data access controls validated by SRE and InfoSec.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Add region_affinity to control plane schema and enable read-only routing for 'europe-west1' tenants in staging.
Phase 2 (ingestion): Deploy routing layer to staging and run shadow writes to regional topics for selected tenants; validate no production divergence.
Phase 3 (pilot): Enable enforced routing for 5 pilot tenants (EU financials customers); run migration tooling in dry-run then cutover during maintenance window.
Phase 4 (gradual): Open UI setting to self-serve for small tenants, require support-assisted flow for enterprise tenants; increase rollout to 20% of traffic per week.
Phase 5 (global): Default enforcement for all tenants that have selected a specific region; deprecate legacy multi-region replication flags after 6 weeks of stable metrics.
migration_steps: Generate tenant audit to identify events retained cross-region and estimate backfill size.
Run backfill worker in throttled mode; validate checksums and event counts against source topics.
Switch tenant routing to new regional topics in a maintenance window, keep dual-write for 1 hour to allow consumers to catch up, then flip consumers to regional topics.
Purge or mark legacy cross-region copies according to retention policy and compliance requirements; keep audit logs for 7 years per legal guidance.
Run post-migration verification job that compares aggregated metrics (e.g., MAU, tokens) between legacy and regional pipelines.
testing_plan: Unit tests for routing logic, including negative tests for forbidden cross-region writes.
Integration tests in multi-region staging with simulated broker failover and network partition.
Chaos experiments: simulate region outage and verify that region-restricted tenants do not leak data to fallback regions.
Load test the backfill tool to ensure we can migrate 10M events/day without impacting live ingestion.
End-to-end verification: QA checks dashboards for pilot tenants and runs regression prompt sets tied to analytics-derived product features.
metrics: Number of tenants with region_affinity set (by region)
Cross-region replication events per hour (goal: 0 for region-restricted tenants)
Ingestion median and p99 latency for region-restricted vs global tenants
Backfill throughput and completion time per tenant
Audit log volume and query latency for compliance reports
notes: Design favors strong enforcement over availability for regulated tenants — documented trade-off with SRE.
We should coordinate with Sales/Account teams for enterprise rollouts; changing region_affinity is high-impact and requires communication templates.
Consider a future opt-in 'replication-exception' workflow for time-limited cross-region analytics during incident triage with proper approvals.
Evaluate using tiered storage to reduce cost for regional retention while keeping quick access for recent windows.
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created and scoped after compliance sync. Initial design sketched with Product and Legal.
2025-02-18: Completed control plane schema changes; mock UI wireframes reviewed by Design (feedback: clarify admin approvals).
2025-02-24: Ingestion proxy tagging implemented in staging; running shadow routing to regional topics for europe-west1.
2025-03-02: Replication worker updated to consult permit matrix; integration tests passing in multi-region staging. Planning pilot onboarding for week of 2025-03-10.
